statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-85231: an authenticated remote attacker can send oversized wrapped data to an RPC service that uses RPCSEC_GSS and make it allocate unbounded memory, because the decode path passed no size limit (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-85231, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2478512). Upstream fixed it in libtirpc commit 65d27459fe569a678cb5cc67d308bcf12c49cb40 (https://git.linux-nfs.org/cgit/steved/libtirpc.git/commit/?id=65d27459fe569a678cb5cc67d308bcf12c49cb40), which bounds two of the three xdr_rpc_gss_buf() decode calls in xdr_rpc_gss_unwrap_data() (src/authgss_prot.c) to 16 MB. Debian lists trixie 1.3.6+ds-1 as vulnerable (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-85231). The DHI Debian repository publishes two builds of Debian's libtirpc 1.3.6+ds-1 for Debian 13. Checked in the shared library libtirpc.so.3.0.0 (libtirpc3t64) of both builds on amd64 and arm64, locating xdr_rpc_gss_unwrap_data() from each build's debug symbols: in the second build two of its three xdr_rpc_gss_buf() calls pass the 16 MB limit (0x1000000), matching the two calls the upstream commit changes, and in the first build all three pass the unlimited value (0xffffffff). The second build's changelog records the backport and the first build's does not. The first build is affected; the range ends at the second.
